back: ATP synthesis using energy released as electrons from reduced NAD and FAD pass along the electron transport chain to oxygen, coupled by chemiosmosis.
H from reduced NAD/FAD → split into H⁺ and e⁻ → e⁻ pass along carriers releasing energy → H⁺ pumped into intermembrane space → H⁺ flow back through ATP synthase making ATP.

front: Formation of water at the end of the chain
Role of oxygen in aerobic respiration
back: Final electron acceptor; keeps electrons flowing so NAD and FAD are regenerated.
Outer membrane, intermembrane space, inner membrane folded into cristae, matrix with enzymes, circular DNA and 70S ribosomes.
Blocks the last carrier (cytochrome oxidase): electrons cannot reach oxygen, chain stops, no proton gradient, no ATP by oxidative phosphorylation.
About 2.5 ATP per reduced NAD and 1.5 per reduced FAD (older books: 3 and 2).

front: Why does reduced FAD yield less ATP?
back: Its electrons enter the chain later, so fewer protons are pumped.
